title: Evening transit cribsheet
content:
Purpose: quick, low-friction notes for the evening transit period (18:00–02:00). This is a lightweight cribsheet — not the canonical runbook. Use it to grab context fast and keep systems stable while I triage the open items.

Quick context snapshot (18:15):
- Production API latency is normal (~95th pct under 220ms) but there was a short spike during the 17:50 deploy (canary).
- Two flaky symptoms to watch: intermittent embedder oom on node pool-b2, and burst of 502s from eu-central-1 edge (prob a routing flap).
- INF-4231 is the active ticket for the embedder OOM; PR 298 contains a temporary resource-bump we rolled out to one canary pod.

Active alerts (priority):
1) Embedder OOMs (INF-4231) — recent tail: 6 events in 20m.
   - Immediate mitigation: scale embedder pool-b2 replica count +1 and increase memory request from 6Gi -> 10Gi for canary.
   - Commands I ran (copy/paste):
     - kubectl -n inference scale deployment/embedder-pool-b2 --replicas=4
     - kubectl -n inference patch deployment embedder-pool-b2 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"embedder","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"10Gi"}}}]}}}}'
   - Note: scaling helped on canary but full rollout is still queued (we must watch for node pressure).

2) 502s from eu-central-1 edge (routing) — intermittent, spike at 17:47 lasting ~3m.
   - Likely cause: transient downstream disconnect to model-serving instances in region.
   - Quick check: hit edge health page and model-serving pods:
     - curl -s https://edge-eu1.redwood-internal/health | jq .component_status
     - kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-server -o wide
   - If >20% pods NotReady, open the eu infra pager (oncall_eu) and add a note to infra rotation.

Temporary routing fallback (manual):
- If eu edge continues failing for >10m and affects >1 tenant with SLA risk, enable fallback-route for affected tenants: set routing policy to cross-region-fallback in console -> routes -> tenant -> edit.
- I toggled this for tenant: beta-shop-2 and saw error rate drop to baseline. Don't forget to revert when eu heals.

Things to watch / heuristics:
- KV cache warmup: after rolling model-server pods, first 10k requests may be slower — expect increased p50 for ~5–10m.
- Autoscaler cooldowns: changes to replica count can take 90s to reflect; don't double-trigger scale-ups unless CPU > 80% for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Node pressure: memory bump for embedder can cause binpack churn; watch node free memory metric closely.

Escalation contacts (evening):
- Primary SRE (me): Ava Chen (DM on Slack, phone +1-415-555-0123)
- Infra lead: Diego Ramos (Slack @diego, pager on infra rotation)
- Model-serving SME: Priya Narayanan (Slack @priya, GH PR reviewer for #298)
- If regional networking: Kate Li (networks team)

Open items to hand off (short):
- INF-4231: verify full rollout of memory bump across pool-b2 and observe for 2 hours — assigned to Diego.
- Investigate cause of eu edge 502s: look at LB config + NAT gateway logs (ticket INF-4275) — assigned to oncall infra.
- Follow up on PR 298: test under load and see if quantization attempt regresses 95th pct latency.

Notes to the person taking over (do this first):
1) Check alerts dashboard (Opsboard > Evening View) and confirm embedder OOM count since 18:00.
2) Confirm canary with bumped memory is stable (kubectl -n inference get pods and check OOMKilled count).
3) Validate eu edge error rate and check route fallbacks status in Console.
4) If you change routing fallback, leave a short Slack note in #oncall-ops with time, tenant, and reason.

Quick recovery snippets (save to clipboard):
- Rollback canary memory change: kubectl -n inference patch deployment embedder-pool-b2 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"embedder","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"6Gi"}}}]}}}}'
- Turn on tenant fallback via API: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API" https://console.internal/api/v1/tenants/beta-shop-2/fallback -d '{"policy":"cross-region-fallback"}'

Cleanup checklist before leaving:
- Confirm INF-4231 has owner and next action (add comment if you took an action).
- Remove any manual fallbacks you set unless there's an open infra ticket blocking revert.
- Post short handover summary in #oncall-handoffs channel (template below).

Handover message template (use and paste):
- "Evening handoff @ <time> — embedder OOMs saw short spike, canary scaled + mem bumped; eu edge transient 502s, enabled fallback for beta-shop-2 (reverted once stable). Monitors: embedder OOMs, eu-edge-502, node-free-mem. Assigned: INF-4231 -> Diego. Ava out at <time>."

Loose questions / TODOs (research later):
- Why did the 17:50 deploy cause a brief lat spike? Need postmortem on canary rollout window. (PR/CI might be clobbering compaction).
- Need a safer autoscale policy that takes node pressure into account (file a GH issue).

Random notes to self (scratch):
- If memory bump fixes OOMs but nodes start thrashing, consider targeted instance-type increase rather than blanket mem bump.
- Keep an eye on nightly batch jobs between 01:00–02:00; they can coincide with lower spare capacity.

End — handoff: grab this doc, add any actions you took under "Open items" before you step out. Cheers and ping if anything smells off.
